result.text: Before going on to chapter 11, I just wanted to go back through kind of our checklist that we got from the first nine chapters and apply that to what we learned in this chapter, in chapter 10, and see how that kind of check those off and make sure that we're thinking about it and applying it and everything like that. Okay, so the first thing is the בינה, the length, width, and depth of בינה and חכמה and all of that, and דעת. And that's just to make sure that this idea of being able to see the relationship of an essence, which is the main theme of this chapter, of chapter 10, and right now we're focusing just on the משל side of it, which means that we're trying to see it in ourselves, in the יחידה and in other things in the world like that. So this should be something that we can have that's very relatable, that we can really directly experience, because it's something that we see in ourself. And and then we want to look for a lot of examples of that. So, on the one hand, we want to see this idea that our essence of our soul is just a single point that who I am like there's a famous story of the צמח צדק when he was a young child, he was sitting on his father's lap, stroking his beard, and saying, "Zaidy, Zaidy, grandfather, grandfather." And the אלטער רבי pointed to different parts of himself and he said, "Is this," he pointed let's say to his arm, "Is this Zaidy?" He said, "No, that's Zaidy's arm. Is this Zaidy? No, that's Zaidy's hand, that's Zaidy's head, that's Zaidy's beard." And so finally he said, "So where is Zaidy?" So then the צמח צדק got off his lap, and he went and he pretended that he hurt himself or something like that, and he called out, "Zaidy, Zaidy." And he turned to him and he said, "Yes, what?" And he said he pointed, he said, "There's Zaidy." So this is an idea that's very relatable even to a small child and can be taught and thought about even on a very simple level, and that's, again, this idea of the length, that we recognize that the real essence of what a person is is not any of those external parts. Those external parts are just the external vessels that it's expressed through. And from seeing that in ourselves, we should be able to then generalize and start to appreciate this idea of the essence and see it in all kinds of other things. But first we have this a little bit of a width where he wants us to first of all see that this is true in each of our different כוחות הנפש, see how the idea of the essence of kindness, and the essence of of justice, the essence of curiosity, the essence of wanting to, you know, win, to overcome challenges, to see how all those things have this relationship that they're really a single point that's beyond any of the details. And then, we also want to understand how there's these two kind of aspects of when when you have an essence, the symptoms of an essence that unites everything, and it it's higher than all the points and it's kind of this bring this out this common theme that unites all the points, all the different details of the expression, and it also permeates each of the details. In other words, that it gives a certain unique aspect to each of the that there's a certain like special uniqueness and value in each detail that is special and unique, that even though they all are united by this common theme, but each one also has a certain quality that nothing else has. And that's another expression of the essence that it gives that to everything. And so we see that again that like you know, there's certain fundamental things that every person wants. Everybody wants to be happy, everybody wants to win, everybody wants to be kind or whatever it is, but there's so many different ways of expressing it, and so we should see that commonality that unites us all, and we should also then appreciate that there's value in each of those different flavors, and that's why we can't do everything and so that's why it's valuable to have all different types of people. And this brings us to the second thing, which is the תבונה, the application of these ideas, and so the applications of this, like we talked about in קוצר ענינים של תורת החסידות, is that number one, every person's essence is pure and nothing can defile it because the essence is this single point that's beyond anything we do, beyond our choices, beyond what we understand or what we feel, it's beyond the שכל and the מדות and the מחשבה דיבור ומעשה, so, therefore, it's not defined by them and it can't be defiled by any problems or flaws in those lower levels. Um so, that's a very important point that it that each we should realize about ourselves and about every other people, that we shouldn't judge ourselves or others based on these lower aspects, based on the שכל, based on the מדות, based on the מחשבה דיבור ומעשה, we should recognize they have this inner intrinsic Godly value just because we have this part of us that's a חלק אלוקה ממעל ממש, a little piece of God, that this spark of our soul has this essential Godly value no matter what. So, that's the first application of it. And the second thing is that it brings out a certain sense of unity that we should see how we're all one. I should recognize that when I look into my essence, I see that these essential human, God-given characteristics are, you know, this really the same as everybody else's, and the main real difference between people is just our circumstances, and our upbringing, and our habits, and our choices, but in essence we're the same. And so I should feel like משה רבינו, who didn't he considered himself it says he was the most humble of any person, he didn't consider himself better even than a גוי עובד עבודה זרה the מיטעלער רבי says, even than a non-Jewish idolater, because he said, you know, if that person would be in my situation, and my upbringing, and have my abilities, then maybe he would have done better than me. Now, how can I compare myself? And it's not just based on a calculation. It's a deeper thing. It's the sense of sameness, that you look into somebody else's eyes and you see yourself reflected in them and them reflected in you. And you see that there's just these external circumstances that separate us. So it gives you this deep sense of unity. And, you know, this is something I always like to mention that I think when we think about how we think about great צדיקים, let's say we think about the רבי, and we imagine how great they are, usually we're we're we're describing that greatness in certain terms that really doesn't fully capture the true essence of who they are and their real greatness. On the other hand, when a צדיק like the רבי looks at even the simplest Jew, even the even a sinner, he sees this essential greatness, this that the fact that God Himself created this person and this is literally a little piece of God. And so he looks with more and sees more greatness and and with more awe and respect at this person, the lowest person, than we look at the greatest צדיק. And we have to train ourselves a little bit to look that way, and and this is the essence of the אהבת ישראל that's brought out by the בעל שם טוב in חסידות, which comes from, you know, looking at this essential value of every person. And actually it goes beyond every person, it goes also to everything, like it says the בעל שם טוב, you know, loved nature, and he saw this godliness in everything, even even just rocks and plants and animals and everything, and having it this, you know, great love for all of God's creations. And this is actually a something that's talked about in the פריערדיקער רבי's work, memoirs, where he writes about the history of ליובאוויטש, and he talks about how it was founded by this fellow מאיר who had this deep love for everyone, and he loved nature, and he loved, you know, all people, Jews and Gentiles alike, and he created this village which became known as ליובאוויטש, which means a city of love, because it was founded on this value of love for all. So again, this perspective of seeing that inner, essential value brings us to to have this sense of unity, and and love, and everything like that. And the other side aspect of it, though, is that also we appreciate the diversity. We recognize that there's a unique quality in every single person, or every single creature in the world, that it's expressing this essence in a unique way that nothing else is doing or nobody else is doing. And so therefore, it's not a you can't measure or compare one thing to another. Each thing just has a unique like you can't say which which is better, this color or that color. It doesn't make sense. They're they're just each one is unique and has its own essential value that it doesn't make sense even to speak of as as comparing them or measuring one against the other because there is no hierarchy. It's just this essential a unique ex- expression of something essential. And so looking at things in that way is like it describes in times of משיח that every single person will be like envious of his fellow, because we're all going to look at everybody and appreciate their unique qualities, which is something that they have that we don't have. And it's again not in a way of competitive jealousy, but in this deeper type of thing, which it talks about in היום יום for the סדר where it talks about the the deeper meaning of the four questions. It mentions it there, and elsewhere also. So that's a little bit of this תבונה, applying some of these ideas to like, you know, more practical things into our עבודה. Now moving on to the next idea of seeing the כלל and פרט. So we're going to get to the נמשל in the next פרק. But then there's the idea of you have to always see in everything we said the big picture, and then the details. And so here, I think the idea of seeing the כלל, the big picture, is this idea of the יחידה, that there's this general essence, which the יחידה or the idea of like משיח that unites everything, that we all have this God-given essential spark that's the same for everything. But then we have to look there's this at the unique way that that essence is expressed in every single level, just like we talked about how the way it is with חסד and גבורה within ourselves and see how that is in every single creature and in every everything in the world around us to find that, like it talks about in קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות that משיח is is not just the general יחידה of the entire world, but he's going to reveal the יחידה in every single thing. And when you reveal the יחידה on all the different levels, that's what brings out all the different unique qualities that he talks about there. And so like there when he talks about how חסידות enhances our understanding of the פשט, רמז, דרוש, and סוד, or he talks about how when the יחידה will be revealed by משיח, how that's going to bring all these other qualities that are going to happen, that we're going to have freedom, we're have the תורה revealed, Godliness will be revealed, all of those are symptoms of plugging this יחידה into these different levels, and that's what יחידה looks like when it's expressed in these different ways. So that's the idea of seeing the relationship of the כלל and the פרט. We have to appreciate the big picture of this essence, which is the idea of יחידה, and then also appreciate what that essence looks like when it's plugged in on each level individually. And it looks different on the level of עשיה or the level of פשט versus what it looks like on the level of, let's say, בריאה and the level of דרוש and things like that. And again, קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות is a very good road map for seeing how to do that, like we talked about when we were learning it. Then moving on to פרק ה, that the idea that whenever we learn any topic, we have to always see the two sides: that there is the אין and the יש. There's the abstract thing that we can't know, and then there's the concrete thing that we can know. And once again, the idea of the essence is something that we really can't know. Even within ourselves, like the אלטר רבי talks about in in a מאמר, beautiful מאמר about this, that we don't know the essence we don't really know the nature of our own soul. We know that we're alive, and we experience it very intimately, but we don't understand it. And that's the idea of anything that's an essence on the anything on a level of יחידה is inherently unknowable. We can experience it, and so, you know, there're even physical examples, he says. When you touch something hot, you feel the experience that this thing is hot, so you know it's hot, you know there's some sort of idea of heat there, but what the essence of that heat is, we don't know. And so this is a very important thing to recognize that we there's a certain unknowable essence there, but then the impact of that we see very tangibly. We see what it means to be alive versus being dead. We see those, you know, the practical implications of that, even physically, in a very simple way of being able to see, being able to hear, being able to move and respond and all these kind of things. We see, again, you know, when something is hot, you touch it, you experience that that how that affects your skin and the sensation of heat, or how it can, you know, burn something or whatever. That's a very tangible expression of the essence of heat, but what the essence of heat is is something that's beyond our direct ability to know. And this is a very important thing to recognize if we look around in the universe on the physical level, on the spiritual level, we'll find that right beyond our reach in everyday things, we very quickly get to this edge of human knowledge where there's an aspect of it that we just can't know. Nobody really knows what consciousness is, they just see the effects of it. Nobody really knows the essence of what gravity is, they just see the effects of it. Nobody knows the essence of what light is, or what an electron is, or any of these things. We don't know. We just know how they interact with things around us and different instruments, and how they react to certain experiments, and we can create mathematical models to describe those reactions, but there's this wall behind which, and that's the idea of like this curtain, behind which there's this unknowable essence. And that's the metaphor of like a king sitting behind a curtain, and the people don't get to see the king, they just hear the messages that are sent or or even maybe the king himself speaking from behind the curtain. That's this idea that the real essence of reality is this is always unknowable, it's always out of reach. We don't really know how another person's feeling, we don't really know what's going on on the inside of them. We can just know how they act on the outside and their facial expressions, what they tell us. And even with ourself, we don't know the essence of ourself. And going back to קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות, that's the idea that חסידות is revealing the אין סוף that's in רדל״א. רדל״א means the רישא דלא ידע, it's recognizing that there's this unknowable essence behind everything and seeing how that's plugging into things. So that's the idea of, again, recognizing this distinction between the אין and the יש. And then in פרק ו, we talked about that this should give us two feelings: we have to have a feeling of humility and a feeling of accomplishment. So on the one hand, we have to have the humility of recognizing that there are certain things we can never know. And so therefore, for example, we can't even know ourselves. We can never judge and fully, you know, say, oh, you know, my own potential. I can't say, oh, I can't do that. How do you know? I don't You don't know the true depth of what's inside of you, and you definitely can't judge others and say that you know what's inside of them. And that's one of the key things the בעל שם טוב talks about, that there's this unlimited potential in every single person, just like there's unlimited potential in the ground. We shouldn't limit that just because on the outside somebody is not learned, or not so religious, or whatever. We can't judge that value. And all we can do, though, is we can try to give somebody the tools, and ourselves the tools and the opportunities to express and develop and cultivate that potential, which is the idea of יש. And we should be proud of those accomplishments, both in understanding and in developing מדות, and in actions, and things like that. And so we should have that sense of humility, but we should also then try to, you know, accomplish understanding and and expressing it, and which gives us a certain sense of flexibility because we know that there's that essence behind it. Okay, then moving on to פרק ז, Chapter 7, we want to see this idea of the יחוד on the level of מקיף, which is the way that when the essence is revealed, how it unites everything and makes and from that perspective, everything is the same. And on the on this practical level, this is the idea of אחדות. We should have a certain sense of unity where we should realize that all people, and really even all things, we should just feel this tremendous sense of unity within creation, And like the רבי talks about, this type of אחדות is the אחדות that relates to שבועות, where all the Jewish people camped at הר סיני כאיש אחד בלב אחד, like one man with one heart, that were all felt that they were the same because this higher essence unites us, and this deeper potential unites us, we all have the same Godly spark. But then that level of אחדות in a certain way is a little bit shallow because it kind of ignores and denies the details of our uniqueness and our individuality. And then we come to פרק ח, which is the יחוד of the פנימי of the which is seeing the אחדות in the פרטים. And that's, the רבי says, is the אחדות of like ראש השנה, where we talk about אתם נצבים היום כולכם, that we're all standing here today, and then it lists the different types of people: the ראשיכם, and the, you know, the זקניכם, from the leaders and the elders all the way down to the woodchoppers and the water carriers. And this is the idea of being able to appreciate how, just like in a body, each part of the body is different, but they all need each other. And so that reveals how they're all part of a greater whole, and each one has its own unique contribution that nothing else has. And from a certain perspective, the head is on top, from a different perspective, the foot is superior to the head, and there's no real way to say which is higher. And so this is the idea of being able to again feel that sense of unity, that we're all coming from the same essence, and therefore, we all have a unique something unique to contribute, which is specific to each person and our situation, our unique situation, our unique, and, you know, wherever a person is, what from one perspective is a מעלה, from another perspective is a חיסרון. What from one perspective is an advantage, from another perspective is a disadvantage. Sometimes it's good to be tall, sometimes it's good to be short. Sometimes it's good to be smart, sometimes it's good to be not so smart. You know, each one gives you advantages for different situations. And so seeing that gives us this deeper sense of unity, which is this idea of a יחוד on a, you know, more practical level. Then the final thing, which is in nine, is appreciating this idea of צמצום, which we're going to really get to in chapters 12 and 13, but we just started introducing that idea. That there's a big, you know, how do you, okay, we have this essence, we have this inner potential, but, you know, how does it actually get actualized? And there's that jump bridging the gap between the two, so we're going to take a look at that. So, hopefully that gives you some food for thought. I'm not saying just to, you know, stop here. I really recommend like taking an idea like this chapter and then trying to look for these connections, trying to look for different examples. Where do we see this relationship of an essence in the world around us? How do I how does this paradigm shift change the way I'm going to look at myself and others, and how would I act differently based on that? And again, we see clues to that or examples of this in קונטרס ענינה של תורת החסידות, where he shows us how this idea of introducing the idea of the essence of the יחידה will change how we look at something like מודה אני on פשט, רמז, דרוש, סוד, and how it reveals the unity between them and everything. And then he also talks about how that relates to משיח and חסידות. So, that's a very good example of all these ideas.
